courses.title: On-Site Training
courses.contact_hours: Credit/work ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Specializes in career orientation and training program without pay in selected businesses and industry, supervised and coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Organic Chemistry I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: CHM 112 with a grade of C or higher
courses.description: Introduces fundamental chemistry of carbon compounds, including structures, physical properties, syntheses, and typical reactions. Emphasizes reaction mechanisms. Part I of II

courses.title: Organic Chemistry II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite(s): CHM 241 with grade of C or higher and corequisite of CHM 246 .
courses.description: Introduces fundamental chemistry of carbon compounds, including structures, physical properties, syntheses, and typical reactions. Emphasizes reaction mechanisms. Part II of II.

courses.title: Organic Chemistry I Laboratory
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: CHM 112 with a grade of C or better; Corequisite: CHM 241 .
courses.description: Introduces various methods and procedures used in present day organic laboratories. Covers the general techniques, organic synthesis, and the use of common spectroscopic instrumentation; synthesizing a variety of compounds; and analyzing the products through physical properties and spectroscopy. Part I of II.

courses.title: Organic Chemistry II Laboratory
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: CHM 245 ; Corequisite: CHM 242 .
courses.description: Introduces various methods and procedures used in present day organic laboratories. Covers the general techniques, organic synthesis, and the use of common spectroscopic instrumentation; synthesizing a variety of compounds; and analyzing the products through physical properties and spectroscopy. Part II of II.

courses.title: Introductory Biochemistry
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: CHM 112 or divisional approval.
courses.description: Explores fundamentals of biological chemistry. Includes study of macromolecules, metabolic pathways, and biochemical genetics.

courses.title: Biochemistry Lab
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides hands on lab experiences designed to reinforce the fundamentals of biological chemistry taught in CHM 260 such as biochemistry assays, enzyme kinetics, enzyme purification, chromatography, electrophoresis and use of western blots.

courses.title: Supervised Study

courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Construction Management and Estimating
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches the equipment and methods used in construction. Includes principles and economics of construction, planning and management, and principles of estimating primarily using highway and building project examples.

courses.title: Principles of Surveying
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week. Prerequisite: Technical Math.
courses.description: Introduces the elements of surveying to include use and care of modern surveying equipment and the application of surveying in construction.

courses.title: Surveying I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week. Prerequisite: Engineering Technical Math or divisional approval.
courses.description: Introduces surveying equipment, procedures and computations including adjustment of instruments, distance measurement, leveling, angle measurement, traversing, traverse adjustments, area computations and introduction to topography.

courses.title: Surveying II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hour per week. Prerequisite: CIV 171 or equivalent.
courses.description: Introduces surveys for transportation systems including the preparation and analysis of topographic maps, horizontal and vertical curves, earthwork and other topics related to transportation construction.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Structural Analysis
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: Statics and Strength of Materials.
courses.description: Focuses on the analysis of statically determinate and indeterminate structures based on principles of statics, strength of materials and geometric conditions.

courses.title: Soil Mechanics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week. (Rev. 5/1/08)
courses.description: Focuses on soil in its relationship to engineering construction. Includes soil composition and structure, weight-volume relationships, sampling procedures, classification systems, water in soil, stresses, strains, bearing capacity, settlement and expansion, compaction, stabilization, and introduction to foundations and retaining walls.

courses.title: Soil Mechanics Laboratory
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces practical soil sampling; classification of unified, ASTM and ASSHTO specifications; laboratory testing of soils to predict engineering performance.

courses.title: Concrete Technology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces properties of Portland cement concrete, methods of mix design and adjustment, transportation, placement and curing in accordance with ACI and PCA recommended procedures.

courses.title: Concrete Laboratory
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on mixing, curing, testing and quality control of concrete.

courses.title: Civil Construction Materials
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the basic properties of Portland Cement concrete, soils and bituminous materials. Includes design and composition, placement, sampling and testing of concrete, soils, and asphalt cements used in civil engineering construction.

courses.title: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: Statics or divisional approval.
courses.description: Introduces the principles of fluid flow and development of practical hydraulics resulting from study of fluid statics, flow of real fluid in pipes, multiple pipe lines, liquid flow in open channels, and fluid measurement techniques.

courses.title: Water Resources Technology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 0-3 hours. Total 2-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the elements of hydrology and hydraulic systems.

courses.title: Introduction to Environmental Engineering
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the engineering elements of water and wastewater treatment, water distribution and wastewater collection systems, solid and hazardous waste, erosion control, and storm water management.

courses.title: Hand Built Pottery
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Studio instruction 4 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces fundamental concepts and skills related to hand crafted hand-built pottery.

courses.title: Wheel-Thrown Pottery
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Studio instruction 4 hours Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces fundamental concepts and skills related to hand crafted wheel-thrown pottery.

courses.title: Introduction to Pottery
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Studio instruction 4 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces art and design related to pottery. Teaches techniques of hand-building, throwing on the potter's wheel, glaze techniques and experimental firing.

courses.title: Principles of Computer Science
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a broad introduction to the field of computer science. Introduces design techniques, development of algorithms, and applications of computer science. Includes the idea of abstraction as a problem solving technique. Examines the functionality of computing innovations and computing systems. Discusses the potential impacts of these innovations from a social, legal, and ethical perspective. The assignments in this course require mathematical problem solving skills, algebraic modeling and functions, and use of variables. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Computer Organization
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: CSC 221
courses.description: Examines the hierarchical structure of computer architecture. Focuses on multi-level machine organization. Uses assembler programming to complete simple projects. Includes processors, instruction, execution, addressing techniques, data representation and digital logic.

courses.title: Computer Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: CSC 221
courses.description: Examines the hierarchical structure of computer systems. Explores the representation of instructions and data, memory organization/structure, structure of a CPU, programming hierarchy and operating system interactions.

courses.title: Introduction to Problem Solving and Programming
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces problem solving and implementation of solutions using a high level programming language in a structured programming environment. Includes concepts and practice of structured programming, problem-solving, top-down design of algorithms, a high level programming language syntax, control structures, arrays, and an introduction into object oriented programming. First course in a three-course sequence (CSC 221, CSC 222 , CSC 223 ). The assignments in this course require mathematical problem solving skills, algebraic modeling and functions, and use of variables.

courses.title: Object-Oriented Programming
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: CSC 221 or equivalent, or departmental consent.
courses.description: Introduces the concepts and techniques of object-oriented programming to students with a background in procedural programming and problem solving. Uses a high-level computer language to illustrate and implement the topics. Second course in a three-course sequence (CSC 221, CSC 222 , CSC 223 ).

courses.title: Data Structures and Analysis of Algorithms
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: CSC 222 or departmental consent. Corequisite: CSC 208 or equivalent.
courses.description: Explores and contrasts data structures, algorithms for manipulating data structures, and their use and appropriateness in writing efficient real-world programming applications. Investigates implementations of different data structures for efficient searching, sorting, and other transformer operations. Third course in a three-course sequence (CSC 221, CSC 222 , CSC 223 ).

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Principles of Public Speaking
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Applies theory and principles of public address with an emphasis on preparation and on the extemporaneous method of delivery. The assignments in the course require college-level reading and analysis of scholarly studies and coherent communication through written reports, including the production of at least one APA/MLA-formatted individual writing assignment. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Introduction to Human Communication
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the elements affecting human communication in individual (e.g., intrapersonal, interpersonal), small group, and public communication contexts with an emphasis on the practice of communication skills in each context. The assignments in the course require college-level reading and analysis of scholarly studies and coherent communication through written reports including the production of at least one APA/MLA-formatted individual writing assignment. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Voice and Diction I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Enables students to improve pronunciation, articulation, and voice quality. Includes applied phonetics. Part I of II.

courses.title: Survey of Mass Media
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the history and current understanding of mass communication. Covers print media (newspapers, magazines, and books), electronic media (radio, television, film, the Internet), advertising, public relations, and mass media theory, research, and ethics.

courses.title: Screenwriting
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the craft of writing for the screen. Examines film and television screenplay structure. Analyzes dramatic strategies in film and television. Learn and apply correct script form and creatively engage in the various stages of original scriptwriting.This course is cross-listed with PHT 120 . Credit will not be awarded for both.

courses.title: Introduction to the Theatre
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys theatre history and the development and participants in the theatrical process. Considers history, process, style and genres, organization, written drama, and performed drama. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Acting I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hour. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to the craft of acting. Covers the practice of physical and vocal warm-ups, improvisation exercises, individual and group scenes, and analytical skills. Develops presence and communication skills. Provides students with introductory exposure to a variety of acting concepts. Part I of IV.

courses.title: Acting II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hour. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: CST 131
courses.description: Extends students' understanding of the craft of acting. Builds on Acting I skills through individual and group text work that include practice listening, point-of-view recognition, personalization, and text analysis. Part II of IV.

courses.title: Oral Interpretation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the theory and practice of performing various types of literature: prose, poetry, and drama. Emphasizes the relationship among the oral interpreter, the literary work, and the audience.

courses.title: Theatre Appreciation I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Aims to increase knowledge and enjoyment of theatre. Considers process, style, organization, written drama, and performed drama. Part I of II.

courses.title: Film Appreciation II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides students with a critical understanding of film through the discussion and viewing of motion pictures with emphasis upon the study of film history and the forms and functions of film. Students will develop skills to analyze the shared social, cultural and historical influences of films and their contexts. Part II of II.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor. May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Business and Professional Communication
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes principles and practical application to effective professional oral communication behaviors to include speaking, listening, and relating, and rhetorical sensitivity within professional, business, and organizational contexts.

courses.title: Writing Across Media
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ENG 112 or departmental approval.
courses.description: Provides instruction in writing and reporting techniques within various professional media fields, to include public relations, advertising, print, broadcast, and online journalism. Focuses on information gathering, developing appropriate and accurate stories, journalistic storytelling, grammar, Associated Press Style, and knowledge of current affairs.

courses.title: Introduction to Directing I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisites: CST 131 -132 or SPD 131 -132 or divisional approval.
courses.description: Introduces theory and practice of stage direction through the study of directing methods as well as the execution and discussion of directing exercises. Part I of II.

courses.title: The Art of the Film
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the art of the film through a survey of film history; viewing, discussion, and analysis of selected films. Studies film techniques such as composition, shot sequence, lighting, visual symbolism, sound effects, and editing.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: Variable hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students. May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor. May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Principles of Culinary Arts I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the fundamental principles of food preparation and basic culinary procedures. Stresses the use of proper culinary procedures combined with food science, proper sanitation, standards of quality for food items that are made, and proper use and care of kitchen equipment. Part I of II.

courses.title: Principles of Culinary Arts II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the fundamental principles of food preparation and basic culinary procedures. Stresses the use of proper culinary procedures combined with food science, proper sanitation, standards of quality for food items that are made, and proper use and care of kitchen equipment. Part II of II.

courses.title: Applied Nutrition for Food Service
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Total 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies food composition, nutrition science, and application of nutrition principles by the food service professional. Provides the student with a basic understanding of human nutrition and application of nutrition in the service of commercially prepared meals.

courses.title: Principles of Food Preparation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Applies scientific principles and techniques to the preparation of food, including carbohydrates, such as fruits, vegetables, sugars and starches; fats, including animal and vegetable, as well as natural and manufactured; and proteins, such as milk, cheese, eggs, legumes, beef, game, pork, lamb, fish and shellfish, and alternative products.

courses.title: Applied Nutrition for Food Service Laboratory
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 3-5 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Includes application of skill sets for understanding, reviewing, revising, scaling, and preparing existing recipes and the creation of new recipes with a focus on healthy cooking techniques, alternative products, and critical thinking.

courses.title: Garde Manger
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies garde manger, the art of decorative cold food preparation and presentation. Provides a detailed practical study of cold food preparation and artistic combination and display of cold foods.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours. Lecture 1-5 hours. Total 1-25 hour per week.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: International Cuisine
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the concepts of cultural differences and similarities and the preparation of the food specialties of the major geographical areas of the world. Focuses on emerging cuisines as they become popular.

courses.title: American Regional Cuisine
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the distinct regional cooking styles of America and its neighbors. Emphasizes the indigenous ingredients, as well as the cultural aspect of each region?s cooking style. Includes the preparation of the various regional foods.

courses.title: Fruit, Vegetable, and Starch Preparation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Instructs the student in the preparation of fruits, vegetables, grains, cereals, legumes, and farinaceous products. Promotes the knowledge/skills necessary to prepare menu items from fruits, vegetables, and their byproducts, and to select appropriate uses as meal components.

courses.title: Stock, Soup, and Sauce Preparation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Instructs the student in the preparation of stocks, soups, and sauces. Promotes the knowledge/skills to prepare stocks, soups, and sauces, and to select appropriate uses as meal components.

courses.title: Meat, Seafood, and Poultry Preparation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides the study and preparation of meat, poultry, shellfish, fish, and game, including alternative protein sources. Promotes the knowledge/skills required to select appropriate use of these foods as meal components.

courses.title: Principles and Applications of Catering
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Analyzes and compares the principles of on-premise and off-premise catering. Includes student presentations in a series of catered functions where they assume typical managerial/employee positions emphasizing planning, organizing, operating, managing and evaluating.

courses.title: Introduction to Oral Health Professions
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Provides an introduction to the oral health profession and covers basic terminology, historical perspective, the credentialing process, accreditation, professional organizations, and legal and ethical considerations.

courses.title: Introduction to Oral Health
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Teaches anatomy of the head and neck, the oral cavity hard and soft tissues, as well as tooth morphology. Includes dental terminology, deciduous and permanent dentition as well as pathology.

courses.title: Dental Science
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies head and neck anatomy, tooth morphology, pathological conditions of the oral cavity, disease processes, and microbiology.

courses.title: Dental Materials
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the materials utilized in the laboratory aspect of dentistry as support in treatment. Emphasis is placed on the characteristics, manipulation, economical control, storage, and delivery of materials.

courses.title: Chairside Assisting I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction on the principles of clinical chair side dental assisting, dental equipment use and maintenance, safety, instrument identification, tray set-ups by procedures, and patient data collection. Emphasis on patient management during restorative procedures.

courses.title: Chairside Assisting II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 6 hours. Total 8 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the student to the various dental specialties including oral surgery, orthodontics, periodontic, prosthodontics, endodontics, and pediatric dentistry. Integrates and applies previous course content to operative dental procedures.

courses.title: Dental Therapeutics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Exposes students to concepts and terminology related to pharmacology, pain control, and dental medicinal agents. Emphasis is placed on the use of materials in patient treatment.

courses.title: Community Health
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Studies topics related to community health issues including identification of specific diseases, symptoms, causes, and effects. An emphasis is placed on the promotion of oral health in the community through patient education in oral home care techniques, dietary counseling, plaque control procedures and application of medicinal agents.

courses.title: Dental Office Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 1-3 hours. Total 2-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Exposes students to and provides practical experience in the legal aspects of dental office management with regard to ethics, jurisprudence, appointment control, recall systems, reception techniques, telephone techniques, accounts receivable and payable, payroll, insurance claims, inventory control, and professional conduct in a dental office.

courses.title: Dental Radiology and Practicum
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches the physics of dental radiation and safety, equipment operation, cone placement for the parallel and bisection techniques, panoramic exposures, mounting and film processing.

courses.title: Dental Radiation Safety
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies techniques and devices used for protection from ionizing radiation. Teaches biological effects, cell sensitivity and genetic effects of ionizing radiation. Includes practice of bisection and parallel techniques on manikins. Prepares employed dental staff to meet the Virginia Board of Dentistry's regulations for certification in dental radiation safety hygiene.

courses.title: Externship
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 12 hours. Total 13 hours per week.
courses.description: Exposes students to the fast pace of a dental practice while they perform support services with an established team.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: On-Site Training
courses.contact_hours: Credit/work ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Specializes in career orientation and training program without pay in selected businesses and industry, supervised and coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Oral Anatomy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the morphology and function of the oral structures with emphasis on the primary and permanent dentition, eruption sequence, occlusion, and intra-arch relationships.

courses.title: Histology/Head and Neck Anatomy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents a study of the microscopic and macroscopic anatomy and physiology of the head, neck, and oral tissues. Includes embryologic development and histologic components of the head, neck, teeth, and periodontium.

courses.title: Management of Emergencies
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the various medical emergencies and techniques for managing emergencies in the dental setting. Additional practical applications and simulations of emergencies maybe conducted to enhance basic knowledge from the one hour lecture component.

courses.title: Oral Radiography for the Dental Hygienist
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies radiation physics, biology, safety, and exposure techniques for intra- and extra-oral radiographic surveys. Laboratory provides practice in exposure, processing methods, mounting, and interpretation of normal findings.

courses.title: Dental Hygiene I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Clinic 6 hours. Total 9 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces clinical knowledge and skills for the performance of dental hygiene services; basic skill components, lab manikins. and client practice.

courses.title: Dental Hygiene II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Clinical 9-12 hours. Total 11-13 hours per week. Prerequisite: DNH 141 .
courses.description: Exposes students to instrument sharpening, time management, and client education techniques and methods. Provides supervised clinical practice in the dental hygiene clinic with emphasis on developing client treatment and instrument skills.

courses.title: Dental Hygiene III
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1- 2 hours. Clinic 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces dental health care for clients with special needs. Includes introduction to computer concepts and applications. Provides supervised clinical practice in the dental hygiene clinic with emphasis on refining client treatment and instrumentation skills, including oral radiographs.

courses.title: General and Oral Pathology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week. Prerequisite: DNH 113 , 114 or 115.
courses.description: Introduces general pathology with consideration of the common diseases affecting the human body. Particular emphasis is given to the study of pathological conditions of the mouth, teeth and their supporting structures.

courses.title: Periodontics for the Dental Hygienist
courses.contact_hours: %Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the theoretical and practical study of various concepts and methods used in describing, preventing, and controlling periodontal disease. Presents etiology, microbiology, diagnosis, treatment and prognosis of diseases.

courses.title: Nutrition
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies nutrition as it relates to dentistry and general health. Emphasizes the principles of nutrition as applied to the clinical practice of dental hygiene.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Practical Materials for Dental Hygiene
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the current technologic advances, expanded functions, and clinical/laboratory materials used in dental hygiene practice. Provides laboratory experience for developing skills in the utilization and applications of these technologies and functions.

courses.title: Pharmacology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the chemical and therapeutic agents used in dentistry, including their preparation, effectiveness, and specific application.

courses.title: Public Health Dental Hygiene I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies and compares concepts of delivery of health care, applying the public health delivery model. Utilizes epidemiologic methods, research and biostatistics as applied to oral health program planning, implementation, and evaluation. Incorporates and applies current health issues and trends.

courses.title: Public Health Dental Hygiene II
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: DNH 226 .
courses.description: Applies concepts of public health program planning through student directed community projects with an emphasis on preventative oral health education. Includes development of table clinics, bulletin boards, and volunteer service in the community.

courses.title: Office Practice and Ethics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Studies the principles of dental ethics and economics as they relate to the dental hygienist. The course also includes a study of jurisprudence and office procedures.

courses.title: Management of Dental Pain and Anxiety in the Dental Office
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: DNH 115 and DNH 120 . Corequisite: DNH 216 .
courses.description: Provides a study of anxiety and pain management techniques used in dental care. Students will understand the necessary theory to appropriately treat, plan and successfully administer topical anesthesia, local anesthesia, and nitrous oxide/oxygen analgesia. Includes the components of pain, pain control mechanisms, topical anesthesia, local anesthesia and nitrous oxide/oxygen analgesia.

courses.title: Dental Hygiene IV
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Clinic 12 hours. Total 13 hours per week. Prerequisite: DNH 143 or DNH 190 .
courses.description: Introduces advanced skills and the dental hygienist's role in dental specialties. Includes supervised clinical practice in the dental hygiene clinic and/or off-campus clinical rotations at various community facilities. Emphasizes treatment of clients demonstrating periodontal involvement, stressing application and correlation of knowledge and skills from previous semesters.

courses.title: Dental Hygiene V
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Clinic 12 hours. Total 13 hours per week. Prerequisite: DNH 244 .
courses.description: Exposes student to current advances in dentistry. Includes supervised clinical practice in the dental hygiene clinic and/or off-campus clinical rotations at various community facilities. Emphasis is placed on synthesis of knowledge from previous semesters, treatment of clients with moderate to advanced periodontal involvement and improving clinical speed while maintaining quality in preparation for practice.

courses.title: Technical Drafting I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-6 hours. Total 3-7 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces technical drafting from the fundamentals through advanced drafting practices. Teaches lettering, metric construction, technical sketching, orthographic projection, sections, intersections, development, fasteners, theory and applications of dimensioning and tolerances. Includes pictorial drawing, and preparation of working and detailed drawings. Part I of II.

courses.title: Technical Drafting II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-6 hours. Total 3-7 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces technical drafting from the fundamentals through advanced drafting practices. Teaches lettering, metric construction, technical sketching, orthographic projection, sections, intersections, development, fasteners, theory and applications of dimensioning and tolerances. Includes pictorial drawing, and preparation of working and detailed drawings. Part II of II.

courses.title: Drafting I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 6-9 hours. Total 7-10 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches geometric construction, orthographic projection, sections and conventions, pictorial drawings, isometric principles, oblique drawing, and dimensioning. Part I of II.

courses.title: Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 0-2 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches use of a positional tolerance system, its relationship to coordinate tolerance systems, and other aspects of industry standard drafting practices.

courses.title: Engineering Drawing Fundamentals I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 4-6 hours. Total 5-7 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces technical drafting from the fundamentals through advanced drafting practices. Includes lettering, geometric construction, technical sketching, orthographic projection, sections, intersections, development, fasteners. Teaches theory and application of dimensioning and tolerances, pictorial drawing, and preparation of drawings. Part I of II.

courses.title: Machine Blueprint Reading
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces interpreting of various blueprints and working drawings. Applies basic principles and techniques such as visualization of an object, orthographic projection, technical sketching and drafting terminology. Requires outside preparation.

courses.title: Blueprint Reading I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 0-3 hours. Total 1-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches the application of basic principles, visualization, orthographic projection, detail of drafting shop processes and terminology, assembly drawings and exploded views. Considers dimensioning, changes and corrections, classes of fits, tolerances and allowances, sections and convention in blueprint reading.

courses.title: Schematics and Mechanical Diagrams
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers interpretation of basic shop drawings, conventional symbols, common electrical and electronics symbols, wiring diagrams, hydraulic and pneumatic symbols, schematic drawings, and piping diagrams.

courses.title: Survey of Computer Aided Drafting
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys computer-aided drafting equipment and concepts. Develops general understanding of components, operations and use of a typical CAD system.

courses.title: Computer Aided Drafting and Design I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches computer-aided drafting concepts and equipment designed to develop a general understanding of components of a typical CAD system and its operation.

courses.title: Computer Aided Drafting and Design II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches production drawings and advanced operations in computer aided drafting.

courses.title: Computer Aided Drafting and Design III
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches advanced CAD applications. Includes customization and/or use of advanced software.

courses.title: Computer Aided Drafting I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches computer aided drafting concepts and equipment designed to develop a general understanding of components and operate a typical CAD system.

courses.title: Computer Aided Drafting II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches advanced operation in computer aided drafting.

courses.title: Computer Aided Drafting III
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Exposes student to 3-D and modeling. Focuses on proficiency in Production drawing using a CAD system.

courses.title: Computer Aided Modeling and Rendering I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 1-2 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on training students in the contemporary techniques of 3D modeling, rendering, and animation on the personal computer. Introduces the principles of visualization, sometimes known as photo-realism, which enables the student to create presentation drawings for both architectural and industrial product design. Uses computer animation to produce walk-throughs that will bring the third dimension to architectural designs. Part I of II.

courses.title: Parametric Solid Modeling I-II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on teaching students the design of parts by parametric solid modeling. Topics covered will include, but not limited to, sketch profiles; geometric and dimensional constraints; 3-D features; model generation by extrusion, revolution and sweep; and the creation of 2-D drawing views that include sections, details and auxiliary. Part I of II.

courses.title: Diesel Engines I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 6 hours. Total 8-9 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the basic principles involved in the construction and operation of diesel engines. Examines fuel, air, cooling, and control system of various designs. Emphasizes engine overhaul and repair, including gauging proper measuring instruments and tools for these tasks. Part I of II.

courses.title: Diesel Engines II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 6 hours. Total 8-9 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the basic principles involved in the construction and operation of diesel engines. Examines fuel, air, cooling, and control system of various designs. Emphasizes engine overhaul and repair, including gauging proper measuring instruments and tools for these tasks. Part II of II.

courses.title: Diesel Engine Reconditioning
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 6 hours. Total 9 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides basic knowledge of the construction, design, and application of selected modern diesel engines and their components. Covers induction and exhaust systems, cooling and lubricating systems, and fuel injection and governing systems. Provides opportunity to disassemble, inspect, recondition, reassemble, and test selected engines.

courses.title: Diesel Fuel Systems and Tune-Up
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 4-6 hours. Total 6-9 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches maintenance, adjustment, testing, and general repair of the typical fuel injection components used on non- automotive diesel engines. Includes engine and fuel system tune-up procedures and troubleshooting using current diagnostic equipment.

courses.title: Diesel Truck Electrical Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week. Laboratory 4 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the theory and operation of various truck and tractor electrical systems. Covers preheating, starting, generating, and lighting systems. Uses modern test equipment for measurement, adjustment, and troubleshooting.

courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to the most basic elements of economics without detailed study of theory. Presents and interprets current issues and concerns publicized in the media. Allows students to understand and grasp the importance of local, state, and national issues with economic themes and overtones.

courses.title: Survey of Economics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours.
courses.description: Presents a broad overview of economic theory, history, development, and application. Introduces terms, definitions, policies, and philosophies of market economies. Provides some comparison with other economic systems. Includes some degree of exposure to microeconomic and macroeconomic concepts. This course applies to career/technical education (CTE) programs. ECO 150 serves both transfer and CTE programs.

courses.title: Economic Essentials: Theory and Application
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents a broad overview of microeconomic and macroeconomic theory with application to current economic situations. Introduces concepts, policies, and theories in addition to models of domestic and global economies. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Principles of Macroeconomics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hour. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the fundamental macroeconomic concepts, theories, and issues including the study of scarcity and opportunity cost, supply and demand, national economic growth, inflation, recession, unemployment, fiscal and monetary policies, and international trade. Develops an appreciation of how these economic concepts apply to consumer, business, and government decisions, and their effect on the overall economy. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Principles of Microeconomics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the fundamental microeconomic concepts, theories, and issues including the study of scarcity and opportunity cost, supply and demand, elasticities, marginal revenues and costs, profits, production and distribution. Develops an appreciation of how these economic concepts apply to consumer and business decisions, and their effect on the individual. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: International Economics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Analysis of the nature, performance and problems of market and non-market economic systems with emphasis on post World War II experience.

courses.title: Money and Banking
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Reviews history of American banking institutions, principles, and practices. Emphasizes the relationship of finances to business structure, operation, and organization. Examines present financial structures, agents, problems, and institutions.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: English Composition Preparation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides academic skills and support for introductory composition. Students will identify and apply academic skills including critical reading, writing, thinking, and research. Upon successful completion of EDE 10 , instructors recommend enrollment in EDE 11 /ENG 111 or ENG 111 or ENG 115 /ENG 131.

courses.title: English Composition Readiness
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Corequisite: ENG 111
courses.description: Provides academic support for successful completion of ENG 111 . Students will identify and apply academic skills including critical reading, writing, thinking, and introductory research.

courses.title: Introduction to Education
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Provides an overview of teaching as a career with orientation to theories, practices, responsibilities, guidelines, current trends and issues in education.

courses.title: Driver Task Analysis
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: Must be eligible for ESL 13 .
courses.description: Introduces the "driver task" as related to the highway transportation system and factors that influences performance ability. Prepares students so they may be eligible to take certification exams for driving school instructors in both public and private schools.

courses.title: Single Parent Families
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Discusses issues surrounding single-parent families and the causal factor including: separation, divorce, death, and teenage pregnancies. Explores the effects on both the parent and the child. Familiarizes students with services available in the community which support the single-parent family.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Foundations of Education
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the foundational topics related to education. Emphasizes the historical, philosophical, social, legal, ethical, and professional aspects of teaching. This course requires a practicum with a minimum of 20 hours of observation in a K-12 setting.

courses.title: Teaching in a Diverse Society
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: EDU 200 .
courses.description: Examines how personal and professional identities, positioning, and intersectional positionalities, values, attitudes, beliefs, and behaviors impact teaching and learning. Develops an understanding of similar and unique characteristics of PreK-12 students and their families, including culture, race, ethnicity, religion, language and learning abilities, gender socializations and sexual orientation. This course requires a practicum with a minimum of 20 hours of observation in a K-12 setting.

courses.title: Classroom and Behavioral Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: EDU 200 .
courses.description: Provides an overview of developing a positive and inclusive learning environment. Emphasizes methods for managing the diverse needs of students in order to promote a positive learning environment. Addresses how to establish and communicate expectations for effective instruction.

courses.title: Human Growth and Development
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an overview of the physical, intellectual, cognitive, language, social, and emotional development of human beings from birth to death, with a focus on birth to adolescence. Emphasizes how hereditary and environmental influences impact the development of the whole child.

courses.title: Instructional Principles of Driver Education
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: EDU 114 .
courses.description: Analyzes rules and regulations that govern the conduct of Driver Education programs with special emphasis on organization and administration. Includes uses in the classroom, driving range and on the street. Prepares students so they may be eligible to take the state certification exam in driver education.

courses.title: Health, Safety, and Nutrition Education
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the health, safety, and nutritional needs of children and developmentally appropriate methods to meet these needs. Emphasizes children's well-being through mindful practices that address health and hygiene, nutrition and feeding routines, childhood diseases, and safety issues. Discusses strategies to promote the mental and physical well-being of children, as well as procedures for reporting child abuse.

courses.title: Foundations of Exceptional Education
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the historical, ethical, social, cultural, and legal practices for providing educational services for individuals with exceptionalities including early intervention, inclusion, adapting environments, and supporting positive behavior. Includes the study of characteristics of individuals with exceptionalities and the influence of culture and environment on development. Focuses on models, theories, and trends in special education.

courses.title: Teaching Basic Academic Skills to Exceptional Children
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops competencies required to teach readiness and basic skills to children with special needs in private or public school settings. Includes the preparation of lesson plans, instructional units, and individualized Education Programs (IEP's). Includes child abuse recognition and intervention training. Emphasizes exceptionalities for students ages 2-21 under Public Law 94-142. Familiarizes students with the indicators of effective teaching.

courses.title: Teaching Online Program (TOP)
courses.contact_hours: Prerequisite: Proficient working knowledge of the current VCCS online course delivery system. Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Instructs educators in the method and practice for delivery of online course content. Includes instructional technology and instructional design theory and practice, with skills and strategies that educators will use to engage students and create a collaborative online environment.

courses.title: Instructional Design for Online Learning
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Prepares educators to design online courses that encourage active learning and student participation. Focuses on instructional design practices including the development of content tied to learning objectives and a peer-based approach to evaluating courses.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Engineering Technology Orientation
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the roles and responsibilities of the engineering team, professional ethics, problem solving with hand calculator and computer applications.

courses.title: Introduction to Engineering
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-2 hours. Laboratory 0-3 hours. Total 1-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the engineering profession, professional concepts, ethics, and responsibility. Reviews hand calculators, number systems, and unit conversions. Introduces the personal computer and operating systems. Includes engineering problem solving techniques using computer software. This course applies to career/technical education (CTE) programs. EGR 121 -122 serve both transfer and CTE programs.

courses.title: Foundations of Engineering
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Total 2 hour per week. Prerequisites: ENG 111 eligible; MTH 162 or MTH 167 , or equivalent; or departmental approval.
courses.description: Introduces the engineering profession and its impact on society and the environment, including engineering problem solving, the engineering design process, and professional practices. Covers fundamental engineering calculations, descriptive statistics, basic spreadsheet and mathematical scripting language applications, professional ethics, teamwork, and communication

courses.title: Engineering Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: EGR 121 or departmental permission.
courses.description: Applies engineering methods to a semester-long team design project with an emphasis on engineering software involving 2D and 3D computer aided design; data modeling and analysis; and iterative programming solutions. Covers design drawings and dimensioning; spreadsheet software usage; mathematical scripting language; and professional practices.

courses.title: Introduction to Computer Programming for Engineers
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisites: MTH 162 or MTH 167 or equivalent; Corequisites: EGR 121
courses.description: Introduces problem solving and implementation of computer software solutions using a high-level programming language in a structured environment. Includes concepts and practice of algorithm design, language syntax, control structures, arrays, and introduction to object-oriented programming. Covers engineering applications, such as mathematical modeling, file input and output, and basic numerical methods. The assignments in this course require mathematical problem-solving skills, algebraic modeling, and functions, and use of variables.

courses.title: Computer Programming for Engineers
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 1-2 hours. Total 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces computers, their architecture and software. Teaches program development using flowcharts. Solves engineering problems involving programming in languages such as FORTRAN, PASCAL, or C++.

courses.title: Introduction to Computer Programming
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 1-2 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces programming in a higher level language such as FORTRAN, BASIC or PASCAL, or C++ on the microcomputer. Uses the operating system, packaged software and peripheral devices. Emphasizes engineering program problem solving.

courses.title: Statics and Strength of Materials for Engineering Techn
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours. Laboratory 1-4 hours. Total 4-7 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents principles and applications of free-body diagrams of force systems in equilibrium. Analyzes frames and trusses. Presents principles and applications to problems in friction, centroids and moments of inertia. Includes properties of materials, stress, strain, elasticity, design of connections, shear and bending in statically determinate beams, and axially loaded columns.

courses.title: Statics for Engineering Technology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces Newton's Laws, resultants and equilibrium of force systems, analysis of trusses and frames. Teaches determination of centroids, distributed loads and moments of inertia. Covers dry friction and force systems in space.

courses.title: Strength of Materials for Engineering Technology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents concepts of stress and strain. Focuses on analysis of stresses and deformations in loaded members, connectors, shafts, beams, columns and combined stress.

courses.title: Engineering Mechanics - Statics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces mechanics of vector forces and space, scalar mass and time, including S.I. and U.S. customary units. Teaches equilibrium, free-body diagrams, moments, couples, distributed forces, centroids, moments of inertia analysis of two- force and multi-force members and friction and internal forces.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Engineering Economics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents economic analysis of engineering alternatives. Studies economic and cost concepts, calculation of economic equivalence, comparison of alternatives, replacement economy, economic optimization in design and operation, depreciation, and after tax analysis.

courses.title: Computer Methods in Engineering and Technology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides advanced level experience in using a computer as a tool for solving technical problems and performing office functions. Includes computer hardware and operating system usage, structured programming in a selected high level language, use of word processing software, computer graphics and spreadsheets. Focuses on the analysis and solution of problems in engineering and technology.

courses.title: Mass and Energy Balances
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: MTH 264 , EGR 121 , CHM 112 (grade of C or higher in these courses)
courses.description: Introduces the field of chemical engineering and how material and energy balances are applied to chemical processes, and physical and thermodynamic properties of multi-component systems.

courses.title: Chemical Engineering Thermodynamics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hour per week. Prerequisites: MTH 265 and EGR 231 (grade of C or higher in both of these courses)
courses.description: Introduces the first and second laws of thermodynamics. Examines energy conservation; concepts of equilibrium, temperature, energy, and entropy; partial molar properties; pure component and mixture equations of state; processes involving energy transfer as work and heat; reversibility and irreversibility; and closed and open systems and cyclic processes.

courses.title: Statics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: MTH 263 or department permission
courses.description: Introduces basic concepts of engineering mechanics, systems of forces and couples, equilibrium of particles and rigid bodies, and internal forces and analysis of structures, including SI and U.S. customary units. Includes trusses, frames, machines, beams, distributed forces, friction, and centroids.

courses.title: Dynamics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: EGR 240 or departmental approval.
courses.description: Presents approach to kinematics and kinetics of particles (and systems of particles) in linear and curvilinear motion. Includes kinematics and kinetics of rigid bodies in plane motion. Teaches Newton's second law, work-energy, and impulse-momentum methods.

courses.title: Mechanics of Materials
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: EGR 240 or departmental approval.
courses.description: Introduces concepts of stress, strain, deformation, internal equilibrium, and basic properties of engineering materials. Analyzes axial loads, torsion, bending, shear and combined loading. Studies stress transformation, principal stresses, and buckling.

courses.title: Mechanics of Materials Laboratory
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines mechanical behavior of bars, rods, shafts, tubes and beams subjected to various types of loading. Introduces experimental stress analysis techniques, such as the use of strain gages and data reduction.

courses.title: Basic Electric Circuits I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches fundamentals of electric circuits. Includes circuit quantities of charge, current, potential, power and energy. Teaches resistive circuit analysis; Ohm's and Kirchoff's laws; nodal and mesh analysis; network theorems; RC, RL and RLC circuit transient response with constant forcing functions. Teaches AC steady-state analysis, power, three- phase circuits. Presents frequency domain analysis, resonance, Fourier series, inductively coupled circuits, Laplace transform applications, and circuit transfer functions. Introduces problem solving using computers. Part I of II.

courses.title: Basic Electric Circuits II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches fundamentals of electric circuits. Includes circuit quantities of charge, current, potential, power and energy. Teaches resistive circuit analysis; Ohm's and Kirchoff's laws; nodal and mesh analysis; network theorems; RC, RL and RLC circuit transient response with constant forcing functions. Teaches AC steady-state analysis, power, three- phase circuits. Presents frequency domain analysis, resonance, Fourier series, inductively coupled circuits, Laplace transform applications, and circuit transfer functions. Introduces problem solving using computers. Part II of II.

courses.title: Electric Circuits Laboratory
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches principles and operation of laboratory instruments such as VOM, electronic voltmeters, digital multimeters, oscilloscopes, counters, wave generators and power supplies. Presents application to circuit measurements, including transient and steady-state response of simple networks with laboratory applications of laws and theories of circuits plus measurement of AC quantities.

courses.title: Digital Electronics and Logic Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches number representation in digital systems; Boolean algebra; design of digital circuits, including gates, flip- flops, counters, registers, architecture, microprocessors, input-output devices.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Computer Engineering
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisites: EGR 121 and either EGR 125 or CSC 221
courses.description: Covers digital system analysis, design, and implementation. Includes digital logic, Boolean algebra, combinational and sequential circuits, hierarchical design, and introduction to computer organization and assembly language. Features in laboratory work the use of discrete logic, programmable logic devices, and hardware description language to design, simulate, implement, validate, and document digital circuits

courses.title: Electric Circuits I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisites: MTH 264 and EGR 121
courses.description: Covers fundamentals of electric circuits. Teaches resistive circuit analysis methods, including network theorems. Features operational amplifiers, capacitors, inductors, resistor-capacitor (RC), resistor-inductor (RL) and resistance-inductance-capacitance (RLC) circuit transient response. Introduces phasor representation of alternating current (AC) circuits. Utilizes circuit design processes, technical writing and computer software for problem solving. Includes laboratory analysis to explore course concepts. Part I of II.

courses.title: Electric Circuits II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisites: MTH 267 and EGR 271
courses.description: Covers sinusoidal steady-state circuit response using phasors, frequency analysis of linear circuits including frequency response, Bode plots, Fourier series analysis, and design of basic filters. Examines Laplace circuit analysis and transfer functions, AC power analysis, nonlinear diode models, and technical writing. Includes laboratory analysis and open-ended design project. Part II of II.

courses.title: Digital Logic
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents an introduction to digital logic, including such topics as number systems, Boolean Algebra, minimization techniques, implementation of digital functions, sequential machines, state diagrams, state tables, and programmable logic devices.

courses.title: Foundations of Environmental Engineering
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: CHM 111
courses.description: Provides an introduction to the concepts of environmental engineering including air pollution, water pollution, water treatment, waste management, and health risk assessment. Examines sustainability and global climate change in the context of contemporary environmental engineering.

courses.title: Hydraulics for Civil and Environmental Engineering
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: EGR 240 or departmental approval
courses.description: Introduces the basic principles governing the statics and dynamics of fluids, especially incompressible fluids. Examines hydrostatic pressure; continuity, Bernoulli, and momentum equations; viscosity flow problems; measuring instruments; and applications to closed conduits and open channels.

courses.title: Capstone Project
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week. Prerequisite: IND 290 .
courses.description: Provides a capstone research project for the final semester of the program, focusing inquiry upon an area of interest to the student or area relevant to their prospective career field. May include problem based research topics, internships, or other focused projects.
