courses.title: Fundamentals of Physical Activity I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents principles underlying the components of physical fitness. Utilizes conditioning activities involving cardiovascular strength and endurance, respiratory efficiency, muscular strength, and flexibility. May include fitness assessment, nutrition and weight control information, and concepts of wellness. Part I of II.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Physical Activity II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents principles underlying the components of physical fitness. Utilizes conditioning activities involving cardiovascular strength and endurance, respiratory efficiency, muscular strength, and flexibility. May include fitness assessment, nutrition and weight control information, and concepts of wellness. Part II of II.

courses.title: Aerobic Fitness I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops cardiovascular fitness though activities designed to elevate and sustain heart rates appropriate to age and physical condition. Part I of II.

courses.title: Aerobic Fitness II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops cardiovascular fitness though activities designed to elevate and sustain heart rates appropriate to age and physical condition. Part II of II.

courses.title: Exercise and Nutrition I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides for the study and application of fitness and wellness and their relationship to a healthy lifestyle. Defines fitness and wellness, evaluates the student's level of fitness and wellness. Students will incorporate physical fitness and wellness into the course and daily living. A personal fitness/wellness plan is required for the 2 credit course. Part I of II.

courses.title: Exercise and Nutrition II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides for the study and application of fitness and wellness and their relationship to a healthy lifestyle. Defines fitness and wellness, evaluates the student's level of fitness and wellness. Students will incorporate physical fitness and wellness into the course and daily living. A personal fitness/wellness plan is required for the 2 credit course. Part I of II.

courses.title: Yoga
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the forms of yoga training emphasizing flexibility.

courses.title: Weight Training I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on muscular strength and endurance training through individualized workout programs. Teaches appropriate use of weight training equipment. Part I of II.

courses.title: Weight Training II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on muscular strength and endurance training through individualized workout programs. Teaches appropriate use of weight training equipment. Part II of II.

courses.title: Lifetime Fitness and Wellness
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a study of fitness and wellness and their relationship to a healthy lifestyle. Defines fitness and wellness, evaluates the student's level of fitness and wellness, and motivates the student to incorporate physical fitness and wellness into daily living. A personal fitness/wellness plan is required for the 2-credit course.

courses.title: Fitness Walking
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches content and skills needed to design, implement, and evaluate an individualized program of walking, based upon fitness level.

courses.title: Yoga II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 2-3 hours per week. Prerequisite: PED 109 .
courses.description: Focuses on the forms of yoga training emphasizing flexibility.

courses.title: Archery
courses.contact_hours: Lecture
courses.description: Teaches skills and techniques of target archery. Focuses on use and maintenance of equipment, terminology, and safety.

courses.title: Self-Defense
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines history, techniques, and movements associated with self-defense. Introduces the skills and methods of self- defense emphasizing mental and physical discipline.

courses.title: Beginning Motorcycle Riding
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies and demonstrates principles and basic skills of motorcycle ridging with an emphasis on safety. Includes basic riding skills, street strategies, protective gear, selection and care/maintenance of motorcycles, and supervised classroom and riding practice. Motorcycles provided.

courses.title: Hiking
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2-4. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces physical and mental benefits of walking or hiking as a form of physical exercise. Skills developed include how to plan for a hike, what to take, and how to select a trail relative to individual abilities. Provides hiking opportunities to explore local regions. Develops awareness of safety, weather, and ecological considerations.

courses.title: Volleyball
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces skills, techniques, strategies, rules, and scoring.

courses.title: Ballroom Dance I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the basic step patterns, rhythmic patterns, and positions in ballroom dance. Includes techniques based upon traditional steps with basic choreographic patterns. Part I of II.

courses.title: Rock Climbing and Rappelling
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents techniques and skills of climbing and rappelling with emphasis on safety, equipment, skills in knot typing, terminology and physical conditioning.

courses.title: Outdoor Adventures I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces outdoor adventure activities with emphasis on basic skills, preparation, personal and group safety, equipment selection and use, ecology, and field experience. Part I of II.

courses.title: Backpacking
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the preparation for backpacking trip, equipment and clothing selection, personal and group safety, ecology, and physical conditioning. Includes field experience.

courses.title: Freshwater Fishing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches freshwater fishing techniques including spinning, bait casting and fly casting. Presents selection and care of equipment, fish habits, conservation, and safety.

courses.description: Provides an overview of the historical, philosophical, psychological, physiological, and sociological principles of health, physical education, and recreation.

courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents an introduction to philosophical problems and perspectives with emphasis on the systematic questioning of basic assumptions about meaning, knowledge, reality, and values. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Logic
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces inductive and deductive reasoning, with an emphasis on common errors and fallacies. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Offers a historical survey of major philosophers from the ancient Greeks to the modern era. The assignments in this course require the ability to write at the college level, read college-level philosophical texts, and understand and apply philosophical concepts with complex meanings.

courses.title: Ethics and Society
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a systematic study of representative ethical concepts and theories and discusses their application to concrete moral dilemmas and social issues and problems. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Biomedical Ethics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces medical ethics with an emphasis on practical moral issues faced by professionals in medicine, public health and related fields. Explores major theories, concepts and terminology in the field of bioethics.

courses.title: Studies in Eastern Thinking
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces an in-depth study of the East through a variety of approaches which include music, literature, drama and cinema. Places special emphasis on Chinese and Japanese philosophy and religion, especially Buddhism.

courses.title: Introduction to Photography
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces principles of photography with outside shooting assignments related to lecture topics.

courses.title: Photography I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 4 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches principles of photography and fundamental camera techniques. Requires outside shooting and lab work. Part I of II.

courses.title: Photography II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches principles of photography and fundamental camera techniques. Requires outside shooting and lab work. Part II of II.

courses.title: Basic Photography
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-4 hours. Laboratory 1-3 hours. Total 3-7 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies fundamental techniques of the camera and its expressive possibilities.

courses.title: Visual Literacy: The Photographic Image
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes photographic syntax, how it has evolved and how it relates to reading images. Examines psychological, perceptual and contextual issues relating to photographic images. Open to students of all disciplines.

courses.title: History of Photography
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys important photographers, processes, and historical influences of the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.

courses.title: Electronic Darkroom
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hour. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches students to create and manipulate digital photographs. Covers masking, color corrections, and merging of illustrations with photographs. Examines the ethical and property-rights issues which are raised in the manipulation of images.

courses.title: Introduction to Digital Photography
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces fundamental techniques of photography, including digital camera operation, postproduction, and printing. Includes technical and conceptual exercises, individual project development, and group critiques.

courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week. Prerequisite: PHT 102 or equivalent.
courses.description: Provides weekly critiques of students' work. Centers on specific problems found in critiques. Includes working procedures and critical skills in looking at photographs. Part I of II.

courses.title: Advanced Photography II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week. Prerequisite: PHT 102 or equivalent.
courses.description: Provides weekly critiques of students' work. Centers on specific problems found in critiques. Includes working procedures and critical skills in looking at photographs.Part II of II.

courses.title: Large Format Photography
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week. Prerequisite: PHT 102 or equivalent.
courses.description: Discusses 4x5 view camera techniques and controls, and sheet film processing. Demonstrates the image-making advantages of large format photography.

courses.title: Outdoor and Wildlife Photography
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches advanced wildlife, outdoor and nature photography. Covers topics such as flash, hyperfocal distance, and maximizing the cameras' digital potential.

courses.title: Studio Lighting I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines advanced lighting and camera techniques under controlled studio conditions. Includes view camera use, electronic flash, advanced lighting techniques, color temperature and filtration, and lighting ratios. Requires outside shooting. Part I of II.

courses.title: Commercial Photography
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines advanced topics relating to commercial photography. Emphasizes advertising, portraiture, and commercial and public relations.

courses.title: Alternative Photographic Processes
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 4 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores manipulated imagery including traditional and non- traditional processes such as non-silver and electronic imaging. Uses enlarged film negatives in order to investigate a variety of methods.

courses.title: Digital Photography II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches theory and practice of digital photography. Emphasizes use of digital cameras in studio and on location. Teaches advanced techniques of image editing. Provides training in digital image transmission from remote locations.

courses.title: Supervised Study

courses.title: Elements of Physics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers basic concepts of physics, including Newtonian mechanics, properties of matter, heat transfer, waves, fundamental behavior of gases, optics, ionizing radiation, and fundamentals of electricity and magnetism. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency, coherent written communication, application of arithmetic, exponents, and algebraic skills such as solving for an unknown variable in an equation, and finding the slope and intercept from the equation of a line. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Elements of Astronomy
courses.contact_hours: 4 Credits. Lecture 3 hours. Lab 3 hours. Total 6 hours.
courses.description: Covers history of astronomy and its recent developments. Stresses the use of astronomical instruments and measuring techniques and includes the study and observation of the solar system, stars, and galaxies.

courses.title: Supervised Study

courses.title: General College Physics I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisite: MTH 161 or MTH 167 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Covers classical mechanics and thermodynamics. Includes kinematics, Newton's laws of motion, work, energy, momentum, rotational kinematics, dynamic and static equilibrium, elasticity, gravitation, fluids, simple harmonic motion, calorimetry, ideal gas law, and the laws of thermodynamics. Part I of II. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: General College Physics II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisite: PHY 201 with a grade of C or better and MTH 162 or MTH 167 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Covers waves, electromagnetism, optics, and modern physics. Includes mechanical waves, sound, electrostatics, Ohm's law and DC circuits, magnetic forces and magnetic fields, electromagnetic induction, ray optics, wave optics, and selected topics of modern physics. Part II of II. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: University Physics I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisites: MTH 263 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Covers classical mechanics and thermodynamics. Includes kinematics, Newton's laws of motion, work, energy, momentum, rotational kinematics, dynamics and static equilibrium, elasticity, gravitation, fluids, simple harmonic motion, calorimetry, ideal gas law, and the laws of thermodynamics. Part I of II. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: University Physics II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisites: PHY 241 with a grade of C or better and MTH 264 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Covers waves, electromagnetism and optics. Includes mechanical waves and sound, electrostatics, Ohm's law and DC circuits, magnetic forces and magnetic fields, electromagnetic induction, AC circuits, ray optics, and wave optics. Part II of II. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Modern Physics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: PHY 242 with a grade of C or better or departmental approval.
courses.description: Covers principles of modern physics including in-depth coverage of relativity, quantum physics, solid state, and nuclear physics.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Supervised Study

courses.title: U.S. Government and Politics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches the political structure, processes, institutions, and policymaking of the US national government. Focuses on the three branches of government, their interrelationships, and how they shape policy. Addresses federalism; civil liberties and civil rights; political socialization and participation; public opinion, the media; interest groups; political parties; elections; and policymaking. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: State and Local Government and Politics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches structure, powers, and functions of state and local government in the United States as related to federalism; constitutionalism; elections; powers of legislative, executive, and judicial powers of state and local government; state-local-federal relations; fiscal matters; metropolitan issues; and policy issues, like health, education, criminal justice and welfare. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through written reports.

courses.title: Introduction to Comparative Politics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teach concepts and methods of comparative politics. Includes empirical analyses of domestic governmental, political, and societal institutions and norms of countries around the world. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Introduction to International Relations
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: ENG 111 or Department Consent
courses.description: Provides an introduction to the causes of international conflict and cooperation. Focuses on the modern state, diplomacy, war initiation, crisis bargaining, international terrorism, nuclear strategy, interstate economic relations, economic growth, international law, human rights, and environmental politics. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Practical Nursing Health and Disease I-II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the pathophysiology, signs and symptoms, prescribed medical and surgical treatments, and appropriate nursing care for the patient with selected disorders. Part I of II.

courses.title: Practical Nursing Health and Disease I-II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the pathophysiology, signs and symptoms, prescribed medical and surgical treatments, and appropriate nursing care for the patient with selected disorders. Part II of II.

courses.title: Normal Nutrition
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Introduces the basic principles of good nutrition. Studies nutrients, their sources and functions, basic requirements for individuals. Includes a brief introduction to diet therapy.

courses.title: Maternal and Child Health Nursing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 7 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines pregnancy, childbirth, postpartum and newborn care from a family centered approach. Covers complications related to childbearing. Emphasizes growth and development and exploration of common childhood disorders at various stages.

courses.title: Care of Maternal, Newborn, and Pediatric Patients
courses.contact_hours: (4 Cr.) Lecture 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Uses a family-centered approach; studies normal and common complications in pregnancy, childbirth, post-partum, the neonate, and children through adolescence. Covers milestones in all aspects of growth and development and common childhood disorders at various ages.

courses.title: Nursing Skills I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-7 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies principles and procedures essential to the basic nursing care of patients. Part I of II.

courses.title: Nursing Skills II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-7 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies principles and procedures essential to the basic nursing care of patients. Part II of II.

courses.title: Applied Nursing Skills
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Applies principles and procedures essential to the basic nursing care of patients.

courses.title: Trends in Practical Nursing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Studies the role of the Licensed Practical Nurse. Covers legal aspects, organizations, and opportunities in practical nursing. Assists students in preparation for employment.

courses.title: Medical-Surgical Nursing I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies etiology, symptoms, prescribed treatment, and experiences in the nursing care of patients with selected disorders. Selects learning experiences to correlate related patient care with classroom instruction whenever possible. Provides observational experiences when available.

courses.title: Body Structure and Function
courses.contact_hours: Lecure 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the structure and function of the body.

courses.title: Mental Health and Psychiatric Nursing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Recognizes emotional needs of patients. Provides knowledge of the role that emotions play. Enables students to understand their own behavior as well as patient behavior.

courses.title: Nursing in Health Changes I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-4 hours. Laboratory 6-15 hours. Total 10-17 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on nursing situations and procedures necessary to assist individuals in meeting special needs related to human functions.

courses.title: Nursing in Health Changes II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4-6 hours. Laboratory 12-21 hours. Total 18-25 hours per week.
courses.description: Continues the focus on nursing situations and procedures necessary to assist individuals in meeting special needs related to human functions.

courses.title: Pharmacology for Practical Nurses
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies history, classification, sources, effects, uses and legalities of drugs. Teaches problem solving skills used in medication administrations. Emphasizes major drug classes and specific agents within each class.

courses.title: Applied Pharmacology for Practical Nurses
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hour. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Applies problem solving skills in preparing and administering medications.

courses.title: Clinical Experience I
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 15-18 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides guided nursing experiences in the hospital setting. Practices skills and applies principles of nursing in basic areas. Includes supervision in administration of medicines. Encourages students to develop basic skills in analyzing patient needs and making nursing decisions. Part I of II.

courses.title: Clinical Experience II
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 15-18 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides guided nursing experiences in the hospital setting. Practices skills and applies principles of nursing in basic areas. Includes supervision in administration of medicines. Encourages students to develop basic skills in analyzing patient needs and making nursing decisions. Part II of II.

courses.title: Nursing Concepts I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 5 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 8 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces principles of nursing including concepts of health, wellness, illness and the nursing process. Develops nursing skills to meet the multidimensional needs of individuals across the life span. Includes computer skills related to the delivery of nursing care. Provides supervised learning experiences in college nursing laboratories and/or cooperating agencies.

courses.title: Nursing Concepts III
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 9 hurs. Total 12 hours per week. Prerequisite: PNE 187 .
courses.description: Teaches nursing care of individuals and/or families experiencing alterations in health utilizing the nursing process. Includes computer and math computational skills related to the delivery of nursing care. Provides supervised learning experiences in college nursing laboratories and/or cooperating agencies.

courses.title: Studies In
courses.contact_hours: Variable hours per week.
courses.description: Covers new content not covered in existing courses in the discipline. Allows instructor to explore content and instructional methods to assess the course's viability as a permanent offering.

courses.title: Supervised Study

courses.title: Introduction to Practical Nursing Concepts
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Total 2 hours per week. Prerequisite: Admission to Practical Nursing
courses.description: Introduces foundational concepts and skills essential for safe, entry-level practical nursing practice. Emphasizes therapeutic communication, legal and ethical principles, clinical judgment, professionalism, and the practical nursing role within the healthcare team. Develops beginning competencies in basic nursing assessment, health promotion, and care planning across the lifespan

courses.title: Patient-Centered Concepts Clinical
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 6 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides students an opportunity to implement classroom learning in a structured health care setting. Focuses on using the nursing process to plan and implement safe, evidence-based, patient-centered care.

courses.title: Client-Centered Care
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 5 hours. Laboratory 12 hours. Total 17 hours per week. Prerequisites: Admission to Practical Nursing
courses.description: Introduces essential physiological concepts that support safe, entry-level practical nursing practice. Emphasizes clinical judgment to provide safe, client-centered care within the practical nursing scope of practice. Focuses on basic care and comfort, pharmacological therapies, and the reduction of risk potential. Develops beginning competencies in medication administration, infection prevention, and monitoring for changes in client condition.

courses.title: Patient-Centered Care I Clinical
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 6 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisites: PNG 110 and PNG 115 . Corequisite: PNG 120 .
courses.description: Provides students the opportunity to implement classroom learning in a structured clinical setting that includes maternal-child health care and adult and geriatric populations. Includes care of the child-rearing family with an emphasis on health promotion and reduction of risk. Focuses on using the nursing process to plan and implement safe, evidence-based, patient-centered care.

courses.title: Intermediate Client-Centered Care I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Laboratory 6 hours. Total of 10 hours per week. Prerequisites: PNG 110 and PNG 120
courses.description: Provides an overview of practical nursing concepts for implementing client-centered care. Introduces the concept of cellular regulation. Expands knowledge of fluid and electrolyte, acid-base balance, clotting, elimination, gas exchange, metabolism, mobility and functional ability, perfusion, tissue integrity, and reproductive sexuality. Focuses on the role of the practical nurse in health promotion and maintenance. Provides an opportunity for students to provide quality, evidence-based care in the clinical setting. Part I of II.

courses.title: Patient-Centered Care II Clinical
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 6 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisites: PNG 120 and PNG 125 . Corequisite: PNG 210 .
courses.description: Provides the student an opportunity to implement classroom learning in a structured rehabilitation or other in-patient setting. Incorporates technical skills learned for the care of complex patients. Focuses on using the nursing process to plan and implement safe, evidence-based, patient-centered care.

courses.title: Inter Client-Centered Care II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 6 hours. Total 9 hours per week. Prerequisites: PNG 110 and PNG 120 .
courses.description: Provides an overview of practical nursing concepts for implementing client-centered care. Introduces the concept of cellular regulation. Expands knowledge of fluid and electrolyte, acid-base balance, clotting, elimination, gas exchange, metabolism, mobility and functional ability, perfusion, tissue integrity, and reproductive sexuality. Focuses on the role of the practical nurse in health promotion and maintenance. Provides an opportunity for students to provide quality, evidence-based care in the clinical setting. Part II of II. [

courses.title: Patient-Centered Care III Clinical
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 9 hours. Total 9 hours per week. Prerequisites: PNG 210 and PNG 215 . Corequisite: PNG 220 .
courses.description: Provides students the opportunity to implement classroom learning in structured health care settings. Focuses on using the nursing process to plan and implement safe, evidence-based, patient-centered care. Provides the student an opportunity to implement care coordination and manage resources to support patient care.

courses.title: Principles of Applied Psychology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the general principles of psychology as they are applied to work, relationships, and growth. Includes perception, learning, development, motivation, emotion, therapy, communication, attitudes.

courses.title: Psychology of Personal Adjustment
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces psychological principles that contribute to well- adjusted personality. Considers the effects of stress and coping with the problems of everyday life.

courses.title: Psychology of Death and Dying
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on psychological aspects of death and dying. Teaches the meaning of death and ways of handling its personal and social implications. Includes psychological, sociological, cultural, and religious views of death.

courses.title: Human Relations
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the theory and practice of effective human relations. Increases understanding of self and others and interpersonal skills needed to be a competent and cooperative communicator.

courses.title: Psychology for Business and Industry
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the application of psychology to interpersonal relations and the working environment. Includes topics such as group dynamics, motivation, employee-employer relationship, interpersonal communications. May include techniques for selection and supervision of personnel.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Principles of Psychology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys the basic concepts of psychology. Covers the scientific study of behavior and mental processes, research methods, biological bases of behavior, sensation and perception, developmental psychology, learning, memory, thinking, intelligence, personality, social psychology, and psychological disorders and treatment. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Personal Conflict and Crisis Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the effective recognition and handling of personal and interpersonal conflicts. Discusses cooperative roles of public and private agencies, management of family disturbances, child abuse, rape, suicide, and related cases.

courses.title: Statistics for Behavioral Science
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisites: PSY 200 and Corequisite: MTH 245 or equivalent
courses.description: Introduces the principles and processes of statistics for behavioral science research. Focuses on selection and application of appropriate statistical tests and accurate interpretation of behavioral science data. Utilizes statistical software for conducting statistical analysis

courses.title: Psychopathology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: PSY 200 or departmental approval.
courses.description: Explores historical views and current perspectives of psychopathology. Emphasizes major diagnostic categories and criteria, individual and social factors of maladaptive behavior, and types of treatments. Includes methods of clinical assessment and research strategies.

courses.title: Social Psychology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: PSY 200 or departmental consent.
courses.description: Examines individuals in social contexts, their social roles, group processes and intergroup relations. Acquaints students with a scientific understanding of how the presence of other people, interactions with other people, and other situational factors influence human thoughts and behaviors. The assignments in the course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through written reports (including the production of at least one APA-formatted individual writing assignment).

courses.title: Introduction to Behavior Modification
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the history of behaviorism and the principles and applications of behavior modification. Emphasizes observation and application of behavior modification principles.

courses.title: Theories of Personality
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: PSY 200 or equivalent
courses.description: Studies the major personality theories and their applications. Includes psychodynamic, behavioral, cognitive, and humanistic perspectives.

courses.title: Introduction to Counselling Relationships
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces counseling theories and provides opportunity for their application through role-playing and supervised paraprofessional counseling experiences. Prerequisite Divisional Approval.

courses.title: Developmental Psychology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Traces development in context from pre-conception to death, including the physical, cognitive, and psychosocial domains. Examines methods of scientific inquiry as they apply to lifespan development. Addresses the interrelatedness of developmental domains, as well as the interdependent influences of environment and biology. Students majoring in or considering a major in Psychology should complete PSY 200 prior to PSY 230 .

courses.title: Life Span Human Development I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Investigates human behavior through the life cycle. Describes physical, cognitive, and psycho-social aspects of human development from conception to death. Part I of II.

courses.title: Life Span Human Development II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Investigates human behavior through the life cycle. Describes physical, cognitive, and psycho-social aspects of human development from conception to death. Part II of II.

courses.title: Child Psychology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies development of the child from conception to adolescence. Investigates physical, intellectual, social and emotional factors involved in the child's growth.

courses.title: Adolescent Psychology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies development of the adolescent. Investigates physical, intellectual, social, and emotional factors of the individual from late childhood to early adulthood.

courses.title: Adult Psychology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies development of the adult personality. Investigates physical, intellectual, social, and emotional aspects of aging from early adulthood to death.

courses.title: Psychological Aspects of Criminal Behavior
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: PSY 125 , PSY 200 , PSY 201 , PSY 202 or divisional approval.
courses.description: Studies psychology of criminal behavior. Includes topics such as violent and non-violent crime, sexual offenses, insanity, addiction, white collar crime, and other deviant behaviors. Provides a background for law enforcement occupations.

courses.title: Psychology of Human Sexuality
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: PSY 200 , PSY 201 or PSY 202 .
courses.description: Focuses on scientific investigation of human sexuality and psychological and social implications of such research. Considers socio-cultural influences, the physiology and psychology of sexual response patterns, sexual dysfunctions, and development of relationships.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Introduction to Physical Therapist Assisting
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the physical therapist assistant student to the field of physical therapy practice and develops basic patient care skills for application in the initial physical therapy clinical experience.

courses.title: Medical Reporting
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes the principles of medical reporting, including the ability to abstract pertinent information from actual medical records. Includes the writing of patient progress notes in standardized formats and medical terminology.

courses.title: Kinesiology for the Physical Therapist Assistant
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the relationship of specific joint structure and function, the role of individual muscles and groups of muscles and neurologic principles in both normal and pathological movement. The course includes a review of basic physics and biomechanical principles applied to human movement. Includes specific posture and gait analysis.

courses.title: Therapeutic Procedures I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 4-6 hours. Total 7-9 hours per week.
courses.description: Prepares the students to properly and safely administer basic physical therapy procedures utilized by physical therapist assistants. The procedures include therapeutic modalities. Procedures may include therapeutic exercise, electrotherapy and cardiopulmonary rehabilitation. Part I of II.

courses.title: Therapeutic Procedures II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 4-6 hours. Total 7-9 hours per week.
courses.description: Prepares the students to properly and safely administer basic physical therapy procedures utilized by physical therapist assistants. The procedures include therapeutic modalities. Procedures may include therapeutic exercise, electrotherapy and cardiopulmonary rehabilitation. Part II of II.

courses.title: Clinical Education
courses.contact_hours: Lcture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 4-15 hours. Total 5-15 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides supervised instruction in the delivery of physical therapy in one of various clinical settings. Emphasizes the practice of all therapeutic skills learned in the first year, including direct patient care skills and all forms of communication.

courses.title: Musculoskeletal Structure and Function
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the human musculoskeletal system. Covers terms of position and movement, location and identification of specific bony landmarks, joint structure and design, ligaments, muscle origin, action and innervation, and emphasizes types of contraction.

courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Psychological Aspects of Therapy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the psychological reactions and sociological impact of illness and injury in clients and their families, and among health care givers who work with them. Examines individual self-identity and the nature of changing client/ therapist relationships across the life span.

courses.title: Rehabilitation Procedures
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-9 hours. Total 5-11 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on treatment techniques typical of long term rehabilitation, e.g., the rehabilitation of congenital, neurological and disfigurement associated with chronic injury and disease.

courses.title: Therapeutic Exercise
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes the basic principles underlying different approaches to exercise including rationale for treatment and may include neurological treatments such a simple facilitation and inhibitory techniques and the teaching of home programs.

courses.title: Pathological Conditions
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents specific pathologic conditions commonly seen in physical therapy. Emphasizes musculoskeletal and neurological system conditions, and all major body systems are represented.

courses.title: Professional Issues
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the health care delivery system with regard to the current practice environment, federal and state influences, laws, and regulations, practice guidelines and ethical considerations which affect the practice of physical therapy.

courses.title: Clinical Practicum I
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 15-20 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction in local health care facilities in the actual administration of physical therapy treatments under the supervision of licensed physical therapists. Provides experience in a variety of clinical settings. Part I of II.

courses.title: Clinical Practicum II
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 15-20 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction in local health care facilities in the actual administration of physical therapy treatments under the supervision of licensed physical therapists. Provides experience in a variety of clinical settings. Part II of II.

courses.title: Seminar in Physical Therapy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Includes preparation for licensing examination, specialized lectures, and preparation of a student project.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Introduction to Radiology and Protection
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents brief history of radiological profession, code of ethics, conduct for radiologic students, and the basic fundamentals of radiation protection.

courses.title: Introduction to Radiology, Protection and Patient Care
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents brief history of radiologic profession, code of ethics, conduct for radiologic students, and basic fundamentals of radiation projection. Teaches the care and handling of the sick and injured patient in the Radiology Department. Introduces the use of contrast media necessary in the investigation of the internal organs.

courses.title: Radiologic Science I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches concepts of radiation, radiography physics, fundamentals of electromagnetic radiation, electricity and magnetism, and application of these principles to radiography. Focuses on X-ray production, emission, and X- ray interaction with matter. Part I of II.

courses.title: Radiologic Science II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches concepts of radiation, radiography physics, fundamentals of electromagnetic radiation, electricity and magnetism, and application of these principles to radiography. Focuses on X-ray production, emission, and X- ray interaction with matter. Part II of II.

courses.title: Principles of Magnetic Resonance Imaging
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ARRT or eligible.
courses.description: Presents concepts of Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Physics. Teaches fundamentals of Magnetic Resonance and application of principles.

courses.title: Radiographic Procedures I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces procedures for positioning the patient's anatomical structures relative to X-ray beam and image receptor. Emphasizes procedures for routine examination of the chest, abdomen, extremities, and axial skeleton.

courses.title: Patient Care Procedures
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the care and handling of the sick and injured patient in the Radiology Department. Introduces the fundamentals of nursing procedures, equipment and supplies specific to radiology.

courses.title: Elementary Clinical Procedures I
courses.contact_hours: Clinical 15 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops advanced technical skills in fundamental radiographic procedures. Focuses on manipulation of equipment, patient care, osseous studies, skull procedures, and contrast studies. Provides clinical experience in cooperating health agencies. Part I of II.

courses.title: Elementary Clinical Procedures II
courses.contact_hours: Clinical 15 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops advanced technical skills in fundamental radiographic procedures. Focuses on manipulation of equipment, patient care, osseous studies, skull procedures, and contrast studies. Provides clinical experience in cooperating health agencies. Part II of II.

courses.title: Elementary Clinical Procedures
courses.contact_hours: Clinical 25 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces advanced technical skills in fundamental radiographic procedures. Focuses on basic contrast media studies, osseous studies, and skull procedures. Provides clinical experiences in health care agencies.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.

courses.title: Radiation Protection and Radiobiology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies methods and devices used for protection from ionizing radiation. Teaches theories of biological effects, cell and organism sensitivity, and the somatic and genetic effects of ionizing radiation. Presents current radiation protection philosophy for protecting the patient and technologist.

courses.title: Correlated Radiographic Theory
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents intensive correlation of all major radiologic technology subject areas. Studies interrelationships of biology, physics, principles of exposure, radiologic procedures, patient care, and radiation protection.

courses.title: Radiographic Procedures II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Continues procedures for positioning the patient's anatomical structures relative to X-ray beam and image receptor. Emphasizes procedures for routine examination of the skull, contrast studies of internal organs, and special procedures employed in the more complicated investigation of the human body.

courses.title: Enhanced Patient Care for Computed Tomography Imaging
courses.contact_hours: Credits 3 hours. Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: The student must be American Registry of Radiologic Technologists (ARRT) certified in a primary category: Radiography, Nuclear Medicine, Radiation Therapy, or ARRT eligible.
courses.description: Applies critical thinking skills including but not limited to patient assessment and care, contrast administration, and radiation safety, as related to those patients receiving Computed Tomography (CT) diagnostic/interventional imaging services.

courses.title: Advanced Clinical Procedures I
courses.contact_hours: Clinical 20-25 hours per week.
courses.description: Reinforces technical skills in fundamental radiographic procedures. Introduces more intricate contrast media procedures. Focuses on technical proficiency, application of radiation, protection, nursing skills, and exposure principles. Teaches advanced technical procedures and principles of imaging modalities, correlating previous radiographic theory, focusing on full responsibility for patients in technical areas, perfecting technical skills, and developing awareness of related areas utilizing ionizing radiation. Provides clinical experience in cooperating health agencies. Part I of II.

courses.title: Advanced Clinical Procedures II
courses.contact_hours: Clinical 20-25 hours per week.
courses.description: Reinforces technical skills in fundamental radiographic procedures. Introduces more intricate contrast media procedures. Focuses on technical proficiency, application of radiation, protection, nursing skills, and exposure principles. Teaches advanced technical procedures and principles of imaging modalities, correlating previous radiographic theory, focusing on full responsibility for patients in technical areas, perfecting technical skills, and developing awareness of related areas utilizing ionizing radiation. Provides clinical experience in cooperating health agencies. Part II of II.

courses.title: Radiographic Pathology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents a survey of common medical and surgical disorders that affect radiographic image. Discusses conditions related to different systems of the human body. Studies the correlation of these conditions with radiographs.

courses.title: Computed Tomography Procedures and Instrumentation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week. Prerequisite: ARRT or eligible.
courses.description: Focuses on the patient care, imaging procedure and physics and instrumentation related to computed tomography imaging.

courses.title: Case Studies in CT (Computed Tomography)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week. Prerequisite: ARRT or eligible.
courses.description: Presents case studies in computed tomography. Focuses on both abnormal and normal studies.

courses.title: Radiologic Specialties
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the study of treatment of disease as it relates to various imaging modalities, computerized tomography, and magnetic resonance imaging. Introduces computers and other innovations in radiology. Emphasizes theory, principle of operation, and clinical application of these topics.

courses.title: Cross-Sectional Anatomy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ARRT or eligible.
courses.description: Presents a specialized study of cross-sectional anatomy relevant to sectional imaging modalities such as computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging.

courses.title: Case Studies in Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MR)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ARRT or eligible.
courses.description: Introduces student to role of collaborator in patient care by providing the critical thinking skills necessary to implement appropriate examination protocols and patient care essential for obtaining diagnostic images. Features cases that can be performed via Magnetic Resonance (MR) simulation or from actual MR examinations.

courses.title: Enhanced Patient Care for Magnetic Resonance (MR) Imaging
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ARRT or eligible.
courses.description: Applies critical thinking skills including but not limited to patient assessment and care, contrast administration and magnet safety as related to those patients receiving MR services

courses.title: Principles of Real Estate
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines practical applications of real estate principles. Includes a study of titles, estates, land descriptions, contracts, legal instruments and concepts, real estate mathematics, financing, agency, appraisal, fair housing, and management of real estate.

courses.title: Survey of the Old Testament
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys books of the Old Testament, with emphasis on prophetic historical books. Examines the historical and geographical setting and place of the Israelites in the ancient Middle East as background to the writings.

courses.title: Survey of the New Testament
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys books of the New Testament, with special attention upon placing the writings within their historical and geographical setting.

courses.title: New Testament and Early Christianity
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys the history, literature, and theology of early Christianity in the light of the New Testament.

courses.title: Life and Letters of Paul
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the journeys and religious thought of the apostle Paul.

courses.title: Selected Topics in Biblical Studies
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines a selected body of literature, a specific book of the Bible, or a pervasive theme.

courses.title: Religions of the World
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the major religions of the world: Judaism, Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, and Buddhism. Focuses on origins, history, basic beliefs, values, ethics, and practices. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Christianity
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the origins and historical development of Christianity, its basic metaphysical and theological assumptions, its essential doctrines, and the present state of the church in the modern world.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Introduction to Radiation Oncology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents an overview of the field of Radiation Oncology, focusing on medical and technical terminology, practices and procedures, treatment charts, roles of staff, clinical objectives, treatment modalities, and equipment. Other topics include patient care, psychosocial issues, ethics and legal considerations of patient management.

courses.title: Therapeutic Radiation Safety
courses.contact_hours: (1-2 Cr.) Lecture 1-2 hours, Total 1-2 hours per week
courses.description: Presents an overview of radiation protection focusing on detection and measurement, shielding and room design, somatic and genetic effects, maximum permissible dose, surveys, source handling, personnel monitoring, and organizations and agencies that guide radiation protection procedures.

courses.title: Radiation Oncology/Pathology I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces malignant pathology arising in each anatomical site, radiation treatment rationale, treatment techniques, and radiobiological response.

courses.title: Radiation Oncology/Pathology II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: ROC 110 , ROC 120 .
courses.description: Continues Radiation Oncology I, which focuses on malignant pathology arising in each anatomical site, radiation rationale, treatment techniques, and radiobiological response.

courses.title: Pre-Clinical Techniques in Radiation Oncology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on basic technical skills in preparation for patient set up and treatment in the clinical setting. Emphasizes simulation and treatment parameters. Focuses on students gaining basic understanding of basic techniques and patient care skills through phantom and lab work prior to direct patient contact.

courses.title: Clinical Clerkship I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 15 hours. Total 16 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces student to clinical setting and the basics of Radiation Oncology. Covers basic technical and patient care skills through supervised direct patient contact and phantom work.

courses.title: Clinical Clerkship II
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 25 hours per week. Prerequisite: ROC 131 .
courses.description: Continues supervised direct patient contact and phantom work with focus on technical skills related to equipment manipulation. With minimal assistance the student should be able to perform basic treatment and simulation procedures as well as patient care skills.

courses.title: Therapy Physics I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week. Prerequisites: ROC 110 and MTH 161 .
courses.description: Focuses on concepts of radiation production, interaction, and influencing factors. Emphasis is placed on atomic interactions and dose measurement techniques. Presents a comprehensive overview of the different types of machines used in Radiation Oncology.

courses.title: Patient Care in Oncology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Total 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the unique needs of the cancer patient, including: site specific side effects, pharmacology, skin care, psychological and nutritional support, and patient care in emergency situations. Explores use of chemotherapeutic agents.

courses.title: Quality Improvement
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week. Prerequisite: ROC 110 .
courses.description: Methods for performing various quality assurance tasks will be discussed, including the medical record component, as well as standards and specification of therapeutic equipment. Allows the student to acquire the knowledge and ability to recognize the inaccuracy of treatment delivery. Reviews warm-up guidelines.

courses.title: Introduction to Cross-Sectional Anatomy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the study of basic anatomic structures and pathologies through digital concepts of medical imaging with emphasis on principles and practices of radiation oncology and diagnostic radiography.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Clinical Clerkship III
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 25 hours. Total 25 contact hours per week. Prerequisite: ROC 132 .
courses.description: Introduces student to intermediate and complex treatment and simulation procedures as well as dosimetry, beam modification devices and brachytherapy competencies. Students would demonstrate proficiency in equipment manipulation and intermediate care skills.

courses.title: Clinical Clerkship IV
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 25 hours per week. Prerequisite: ROC 231 .
courses.description: Students perform intermediate procedures with minimal assistance and demonstrate comprehension of tasks related to complex procedures. During this clerkship the student should demonstrate the ability to work more independently.

courses.title: Therapy Physics II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week. Prerequisite: ROC 141 .
courses.description: Studies methods and devices used for measurement of and protection from ionizing radiation. Discusses types of brachytherapy applicators and dose distributions systems and includes brachytherapy dose calculation exercises. Introduces electron beam dosimetry.

courses.title: Clinical Radiobiology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week. Prerequisites: ROC 110 , ROC 120 and ROC 121 .
courses.description: Covers an advanced study into the principles of biologic responses to radiation. Focuses on the events that occur following absorption of energy from radiation at the cellular, tissue, and systemic whole body levels, and factors that influence the effects.

courses.title: Dosimetry Planning
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week. Prerequisites: ROC 110 and MTH 161 .
courses.description: Introduces clinical dosimetry and treatment planning to include various treatment techniques, calculations, equations, and beam arrangements.

courses.title: Professional Seminar
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Corequisite: All Radiation Oncology Core Courses.
courses.description: Correlates all major radiation oncology subject areas in preparation for national certification.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Introduction to Recreation, Parks & Leisure Studies
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Includes history and philosophy of the Recreation and Parks movement. Discusses the theory of leisure and play. Analyzes leisure service delivery systems and career opportunities. Emphasizes the commercial, non-profit and public sectors, Armed Forces, therapeutic recreation as well as volunteer service.

courses.title: Outdoor Recreation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Includes history and philosophy of conservation, preservation, and the development of outdoor recreation in the United States. Emphasizes development of practical skills in planning, instructing, and managing outdoor recreation programs and facilities, including youth resident camps, R.V. campgrounds, as well as resources in the urban setting.

courses.title: Wilderness First Aid
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the role of outdoor professionals in wilderness medicine and the response, care and rescue of outdoor participants in non-urban environments. Provides intensive, in-depth training in the areas of cardio-pulmonary resuscitation, patient assessment system, body systems, environmental injuries/ conditions, anaphylaxis, lifting/moving/extrication, patient carries, and backcountry medicine.

courses.title: Fund. Theory and Procedures for Respiratory Care
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week. 3-4 Credits This is a first semester course that requires acceptance into the Respiratory Therapy program.
courses.description: Focuses on the development of basic respiratory care skills necessary to enter the hospital environment.

courses.title: Anatomy & Physiology of the Cardiopulmonary System
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Concentrates on anatomy and physiology of the cardio- pulmonary system.

courses.title: Pathology of the Cardiopulmonary System
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents pathophysiology of medical and surgical diseases with emphasis upon diseases of cardiopulmonary system.

courses.title: Cardiopulmonary Science I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on pathophysiology, assessment, treatment, and evaluation of patients with cardiopulmonary disease. Explores cardiopulmonary and neuromuscular physiology and patho- physiology.

courses.title: Respiratory Care Theory and Procedures II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents theory of equipment and procedures and related concepts used for patients requiring general, acute and critical cardiopulmonary care. Part II of II.

courses.title: Pharmacology for Respiratory Care I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents selection criteria for the use of, and detailed information on pharmacologic agents used in pulmonary care.

courses.title: Fundamental Clinical Procedures I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Offers clinical instruction in basic patient care practices.

courses.title: Fundamental Clinical Procedures II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Offers clinical instruction in basic patient care practices.

courses.title: Pulmonary Rehabilitation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Focuses on purpose and implementation of comprehensive pulmonary rehabilitation program.

courses.title: Cardiopulmonary Science II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on assessment, treatment, and evaluation of patients with cardiopulmonary disease. Explores cardiopulmonary, renal, and neuromuscular physiology, and pathophysiology.

courses.title: Neonatal and Pediatric Respiratory Procedures
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the cardiopulmonary, physiology, pathology and application of therapeutic procedures in the management of the newborn and pediatric patient.

courses.title: Pharmacology for Respiratory Care II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Concentrates on pharmacologic agents used in the management of the critically ill patient.

courses.title: Advanced Clinical Procedures III
courses.contact_hours: Clinical 15-20 hours per week.
courses.description: Offers clinical instruction in advanced patient care practices.

courses.title: Beginning Russian I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills and emphasizes basic sentence structure. Part I of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Beginning Russian II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisites: RUS 101 , or two years of successful completion of high school Russian, or demonstrated experiential learning, or by placement test, or equivalent.
courses.description: Develops the understanding, speaking, reading, and writing of Russian, and emphasizes the structure of the language. May include oral drill and practice. Part II of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Intermediate Russian I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: RUS 102 , or three years of successful completion of high school Russian, or demonstrated experiential learning, or by placement test, or equivalent.
courses.description: Continues to develop cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills, and introduces complex sentence structures. Classes may be conducted in target language. Part I of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Intermediate Russian II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: RUS 201 , or four years of successful completion of high school Russian, or demonstrated experiential learning, or by placement test, or equivalent.
courses.description: Continues to develop cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills, and emphasizes complex sentence structures. Classes may be conducted in the target language. Part II of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Motorcycle Rider Safety - Beginner
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 1-2 hours. Total 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies principles and basic skills of motorcycle riding with an emphasis on safety. Includes street strategies, protective gear, and selection and care/maintenance of motorcycles.

courses.title: Safety & Health Standards: Regulations and Codes
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches development of safety standards, the Occupational Safety and Health Act (OSHA), its rules and regulations; penalties for non-compliance, and methods of compliance. Includes an examination of Government Regulatory Codes and appraisal of consensus, advisory, and proprietary standards.

courses.title: Principles of Industrial Safety
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches principles and practices of accident prevention, analysis of accident causes, mechanical safeguards, fire prevention, housekeeping, occupational diseases, first aid, safety organization, protection equipment and general safety principles and promotion.

courses.title: Industrial Safety
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides basic understanding of safety and health in an industrial situation. Includes hazardous materials, substances, conditions, activities and habits as well as the prescribed methods and equipment needed for the apprentice to protect himself/herself and others.

courses.title: Construction Safety - OSHA 10
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Total 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Presents an introduction to occupational health and safety and its application on the construction site. Introduces the safety standards of the Occupational Safety and Health Act (OSHA), its rules and regulations with emphasis of recognizing job-site hazards (OSHA 10 for Construction).

courses.title: Safety Program Organization and Administration
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces techniques of organizing and administering practical safety programs. Emphasizes safety as a management function. Includes an examination of history, occupational safety and health regulations, and a survey of current laws, codes and standards.

courses.title: Introduction to Environmental and Science Technology I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the basic sciences which describe our physical environment. Includes the fundamentals of geology, meteorology, physics, chemistry, and biology. Describes basic scientific principles and relates them to natural phenomena and the activities of man. Emphasizes field experiences including techniques and data gathering. Part I of II.

courses.title: Introduction to Environmental and Science Technology II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the basic sciences which describe our physical environment. Includes the fundamentals of geology, meteorology, physics, chemistry, and biology. Describes basic scientific principles and relates them to natural phenomena and the activities of man. Emphasizes field experiences including techniques and data gathering. Part II of II.

courses.title: College Success Skills
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-3 hours. Total 1-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Assists students in transition to colleges. Provides overviews of college policies, procedures, curricular offerings. Encourages contacts with other students and staff. Assists students toward college success through information regarding effective study habits, career and academic planning, and other college resources available to students. May include English and Math placement testing. Strongly recommended for beginning students. Required for graduation.

courses.title: Orientation To (Specify the Discipline)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-3 hours. Total 1-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to the skills which are necessary to achieve their academic goals, to services offered at the college and to the discipline in which they are enrolled. Covers topics such as services at the college including the learning resources center; counseling, and advising; listening, test taking, and study skills; and topical areas which are applicable to their particular discipline or background.

courses.title: Study Skills
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Assists students in planning strategies to overcome nonproductive study habits and in implementing positive study behaviors. Includes management, memory improvement, note taking, and test taking.

courses.title: Preparation for Employment
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides experience in resume writing, preparation of applications, letters of application, and successfully preparing for and completing the job interview. Assists students in identifying their marketable skills and aptitudes. Develops strategies for successful employment search. Assists students in understanding effective human relations techniques and communication skills in job search.

courses.title: Career Education
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys career options available to students. Stresses career development and assists in the understanding of self in the world of work. Assists students in applying decision-making to career choice.

courses.title: College Survival Skills
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-3 hours. Total 1-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an orientation to the college. Introduces study skills, career and life planning. Offers an opportunity to engage in activities aimed at self-discovery. Emphasizes development of "coping skills" such as listening, interpersonal relations, competence, and improved self-concept. Recommended for students enrolled in developmental courses.

courses.title: Student Leadership Development
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides opportunities for student to learn leadership theory and skills for application in campus organizations, committees and groups.
